messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: PD-98321 -> severity: high (auto-escalation). Multiple 5xx spikes observed from az2 in us-west-2 region. Automated routing divert to az1 initiated. Notifying on-call.
Marc: acked via PagerDuty. I’m looking at the network telemetry now. :eyes:
Sara: I’m on call for infra — joining. Any customer-facing errors reported yet? Can we confirm ingress packet drops?
Marc: seeing elevated TCP retransmits to the model-shard hosts in az2, nodes reporting NIC errors. Quick check:
```
# from monitoring node
kubectl -n infra logs nic-monitor-az2 | tail -n 200
[2026-03-15T22:04:12Z] NIC_ERR: device eth0 rx_errors=482 tx_errors=0
[2026-03-15T22:04:13Z] LINK_FLAP: eth0 down -> up
[2026-03-15T22:04:15Z] PACKET_DROP: 1m avg 28%
```
Marc: autoscaler paused for az2 to avoid flapping; traffic is being diverted but some in-flight gradient requests failed with 502s. We should rate-limit new heavy model jobs in affected AZ.
Tariq: oncall-runtime here. Can we trigger fallback to the lighter quantized model in az1 + az3 to reduce per-req CPU while diversion continues? That should keep latency stable for most customers.
Kelly: Product & support - brief: we have a handful of errors hitting enterprise customers' logs; SLO alerting showing increased tail latency. Please annotate customer impact ASAP; CS will need the initial stmt.
Sara: spinning up a rapid fallback plan: route policy change -> prefer az1/az3, force-model-variant=redwood-small-8q, enable-prefix-kv-cache-evict=false. Applying now.
deploy-bot: runbook trigger: applied routing-policy "az2-divert-az1-az3" at 22:06 UTC by Sara. Link: https://console.internal/redwood/runbooks/az-divert
Marc: after routing change, 5xx rate down from 6% -> 1.2% over last 3m. Latency tail still elevated (p99 ~ 1.9s). Looks like partial recovery.
Sara: NIC errors persist on host group az2-rack-4. Opening fabric ticket with datacenter ops. Tagging @datacenter-ops. 
Marc: PD escalation to level2 already in progress (PD-98321 -> EngSRE team). ETA for physical remediation unknown.
Tariq: I'm switching model stepdown on the traffic router: prefer quant-8 -> enabling aggressive KV cache on az1/az3 to lower token generation CPU.
Kelly: CS: notifying affected accounts with initial blurb: "We’re experiencing degraded performance in one AZ impacting API errors/latency for a subset of requests. Traffic is diverted and mitigation is underway. No request data exposed." Will post a status page update after final notes.
Marc: handoff in 30m to Tariq for ongoing remediation. Notes for handoff:
- root cause: NIC hardware errors presenting as rx_errors and link flaps
- impact: increased 5xx and p99 latency for keys routed to az2; small percentage of in-flight requests failing
- mitigations applied: routing divert -> az1/az3, model variant stepdown, autoscaler suspended for az2 hosts
- runbook: https://console.internal/redwood/runbooks/az-divert
Sara: datacenter ops response: "We see a burst of CRC errors on leaf-switch port, investigating upstream optics. Will confirm hardware swap ETA 40-70m." (from DC ticket #DC-4271)
Tariq: oncall takeover: I’ll monitor the diverted traffic and coordinate the rollback once DC confirms patch. I’ll also keep the light model in the pool until we validate p99 under 1.2s for 15m.
Marc: quick checklist run while handing off:
- [x] pager acknowledged
- [x] routing divert applied
- [x] model stepdown applied
- [x] autoscaler paused in az2
- [x] DC ticket opened
- [ ] hardware swap complete
- [ ] traffic rollback validated
Sara: putting short status update on status.redwood.com -> "Partial outage: one AZ experiencing network degradation; traffic diverted; mitigations in place. Engineers are working." ETA next update in 20m. :loud_sound:
deploy-bot: auto note: PD-98321 escalation -> L2 pinged; incident channel created: #incident-pd-98321
Kelly: CS prepping email to top-tier customers. I’ll paste draft here for review before sending.
Kelly: draft: "We experienced degraded API availability for a subset of requests routed through a single AZ. We have diverted traffic and are operating on fallback models to maintain availability while we replace faulty hardware. We will follow up with a full post-incident summary once remediation completes." Need approval to send now?
Marc: approved. Send it out, mark severity as 'reduced impact' in the status update.
Tariq: monitoring: p50/p90 stable, p99 trending down. Will keep watch and post when DC confirms swap. If swap goes >90m, we should plan a controlled draining of az2 and permanent divert until maintenance window.
Sara: DC confirms they have the replacement optics on site, tech prepping for hot-swap. Good sign.
Marc: leaving final runbook notes in the incident doc and passing active ownership to Tariq. I’ll be reachable if escalation needed. :thumbsup:
Tariq: taking over. I’ll post updates every 15m or on state changes. Closing on-call handoff now.
incident-bot: PD-98321 status changed -> acknowledged by Marc (22:05 UTC), assigned to EngSRE, owner: Tariq. Auto-closure scheduled after 8 hours of inactivity.
Tariq: post-swap check will include:
1) NIC link stability for az2 hosts
2) token generation p99 under 1.2s for 20m
3) <1% 5xx across the fleet
If all good, rollback traffic divert and resume autoscaler.
Sara: thanks team. Good coordination. I’ll follow DC ticket and close when hardware confirmed.
deploy-bot: runbook note appended: "Applied model-variant stepdown and routing divert; monitor p99 and 5xx. Handoff to Tariq at 22:18 UTC." 
Kelly: CS update sent to customers and status page updated.
Tariq: update 22:48 UTC - DC reports swap complete, initial metrics look stable, scheduling gradual rollback in 10m. Will abort if 5xx spikes or link flaps reappear.
Marc: thx. Keep rollback gradual and watch for in-flight error types.
Tariq: rollback started at 22:59 UTC. Monitoring closely.
Sara: 23:05 UTC - rollback looks clean, p99 holding at 1.0s, 5xx <= 0.4% fleet-wide.
Tariq: confirming: az2 healthy. Re-enable autoscaler and remove routing divert. Closing incident PD-98321 and archiving notes in the incident doc.
incident-bot: PD-98321 -> resolved by Tariq at 23:12 UTC. Summary: NIC optics failure in az2; traffic diverted and fallback models used; hardware swap resolved; no data exposure; postmortem planned.
Kelly: opening customer follow-up with timeline + next steps for customers wanting extra SLAs. Will coordinate on the postmortem.
Marc: filing postmortem, linking logs and DC ticket. Good job everyone. :clap:
